caveats.title: Caveats
caveats.description: The traps THESE numbers trigger, already written out. Derived from the fields of this same response — `score`, `review_count`, `concentration`, `self_rated` — never from a second query. **Advisory: it never moves the score and never fills a null one.** An empty list means no trap fired, NOT 'verified clean'. Spanish prose, same rules as the wallet route, from the same module. Each entry is `{code, text}`: branch on `code`, never on `text`.

ratings.title: Ratings
ratings.description: **Every** rating this agent received, one row each, revoked and out-of-domain included, each with its `tx_hash`, block and log index. This is what the price buys: not a number, the population that produced it. It can be very long — the loudest agent in this index carries 300,001 rows, measured 2026-08-11.

policy_version.title: Policy Version
policy_version.description: The aggregation policy that produced these numbers. Travels in every scored response; also published free in `GET /health`.

AgentScore.title: AgentScore
AgentScore.description:
One agent identity and EVERY rating it received.

The most detailed thing this API sells: not a number but the population
that produced it, row by row, with the transaction behind each one and the
revoked ones included. `caveats` comes BEFORE `ratings` on purpose — that
list can carry 300,001 rows, and a warning that only shows up after it is a
warning nobody reads.

code.title: Code
code.description: Stable identifier of the trap that fired. Branch on THIS, never on `text`. Codes are permanent; text is not.

text.title: Text
text.description: Spanish prose meant to be shown to whoever is deciding. May be rewritten, re-measured or translated without notice.

Caveat.title: Caveat
Caveat.description:
Una trampa que ESTOS números disparan, con su código estable.

🔴 `code` ES EL CONTRATO; `text` NO. El texto puede re-redactarse,
re-medirse o traducirse sin aviso — el código nunca cambia. Nace del hueco
H14 del 2026-08-28: los tres consumidores del ecosistema (Execution Market,
KarmaKadabra, MeshRelay) fueron instruidos ese mismo día de MOSTRAR estas
advertencias, y lo único que tenían para ramificar era la prosa. El texto ya
se había movido una vez (el corte de evidencia flaca, el 2026-08-25) y
cualquiera colgado de esa prosa se rompió ese día sin enterarse.

Se cambió la forma AHORA y no después a propósito: es el momento más barato
de la vida del proyecto para hacerlo — los tres consumidores están migrando
y ninguno construyó todavía contra la forma vieja. Dentro de dos semanas el
mismo cambio rompe tres integraciones vivas.

raters.title: Raters
raters.description: Distinct wallets that wrote them. Read together with `ratings`: the gap between the two is the shape of the activity.

ChainDay.title: ChainDay
ChainDay.description: One day of activity on a chain, by on-chain time.

ChainDetail.title: ChainDetail
ChainDetail.description: Everything we can say about one chain: totals, top wallets and facets.

facet.title: Facet
facet.description: Area of reputation, as the raters declared it in `tag1`.

count.title: Count
count.description: Ratings in this area on this chain.

distinct_agents.title: Distinct Agents
distinct_agents.description: How many different subjects were rated in this area. A facet concentrated on one subject is not a facet of the chain.

distinct_raters.title: Distinct Raters
distinct_raters.description: How many different wallets did the rating here.

avg_score.title: Avg Score
avg_score.description: Mean over this area, or **null** when there is nothing to average. Never zero for absent.

ChainFacet.title: ChainFacet
ChainFacet.description: One area of reputation aggregated over a whole chain.

rank.title: Rank
rank.description: Position in this chain's ranking, ordered by `shrunk_score` — not by `final_score`.

final_score.title: Final Score
final_score.description: Mean score **on this chain**, not the global one. They are different numbers: the global averages this wallet's per-chain means. Null when there is nothing to average.

shrunk_score.title: Shrunk Score
shrunk_score.description: What decides the position: the score pulled toward this network's prior by how little evidence backs it. **This orders the index; it is not the score we publish about a wallet.** A perfect 100 from one rater ranks below an 85 from four.

distinct_raters.title: Distinct Raters
distinct_raters.description: Distinct rating wallets. The number that separates evidence from a campaign.

agent_count.title: Agent Count
agent_count.description: ERC-8004 identities this wallet owns on this chain.

declared_types.title: Declared Types
declared_types.description: What the identities SAY they are, verbatim from their own card. We never verify it — a declaration is not a fact, and null entries are identities that declared nothing.

ChainRow.title: ChainRow
ChainRow.description: Una wallet dentro de UNA cadena.

score.title: Score
score.description: Mean over this chain's eligible ratings, 0-100. Null, never 0, when none are eligible here.

review_count.title: Review Count
review_count.description: Eligible ratings on this chain — the N behind `score`.

agent_ids.title: Agent Ids
agent_ids.description: The identities this wallet owns on this chain that carry those ratings. Each one is callable at `GET /reputation/agent/{network}/{agent_id}` for the row-by-row breakdown.

ChainScore.title: ChainScore
ChainScore.description:
What one chain contributed to a wallet's score.

Published per chain and never collapsed: the wallet score is the mean of
these, one vote each, so this is the breakdown that lets the mean be
recomputed by hand.

network.title: Network
network.description: Chain name — the exact vocabulary every `{network}` path and query parameter in this API accepts.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: Agent identities indexed on this chain.

owners.title: Owners
owners.description: Distinct current owners behind those identities. Far below `agents` means a few wallets hold many ids.

typed_agents.title: Typed Agents
typed_agents.description: How many of them declare a type. The rest declare none — a fact about the chain's population, not a gap in the index.

ratings.title: Ratings
ratings.description: Individual ratings indexed on this chain, eligible or not.

distinct_raters.title: Distinct Raters
distinct_raters.description: **How many wallets spoke, not how many times.** This is the column that makes `avg_value` readable: avalanche averages 76.95 and base 22.95, and whoever reads only those two concludes avalanche is better — avalanche's mean comes from ELEVEN raters with one of them writing 64% of it, base's from 12,624.

revoked.title: Revoked
revoked.description: Ratings taken back by their rater, on this chain.

orphan_ratings.title: Orphan Ratings
orphan_ratings.description: Ratings pointing at an agent this index does NOT have registered. A health metric of our own indexer, published as public data on purpose: it was the only thing that exposed one chain sitting at 0.1% coverage. Whoever integrates deserves to know how complete what we sell them is.

facets.title: Facets
facets.description: Distinct `tag1` areas seen on this chain.

out_of_domain.title: Out Of Domain
out_of_domain.description: Ratings whose normalized value fell outside `0 < v <= 100` and are therefore excluded from every score.

self_rated.title: Self Rated
self_rated.description: Ratings written by the rated agent's own owner. Excluded from scores.

avg_value.title: Avg Value
avg_value.description: Mean normalized value across eligible ratings. **Never read it alone** — `distinct_raters` and `top_rater_share` sit in this same object precisely so it cannot be. Null when nothing is eligible.

top_rater_share.title: Top Rater Share
top_rater_share.description: Percentage of this chain's ratings written by its single loudest rater. Advisory. Null with no ratings.

ratings_per_agent.title: Ratings Per Agent
ratings_per_agent.description: Ratings divided by agents. High here is repetition, not consensus — the same read as `distinct_raters` at wallet level.

first_rating_at.title: First Rating At
first_rating_at.description: Oldest rating by on-chain time. Null until the log scan dates one.

last_rating_at.title: Last Rating At
last_rating_at.description: Newest rating by on-chain time. Null until the log scan dates one.

last_scanned_block.title: Last Scanned Block
last_scanned_block.description: How far the scan reached. On signature-scanned chains (solana) it carries the slot. Null before the first sync.

blocks_behind.title: Blocks Behind
blocks_behind.description: `head_at_last_sync - last_scanned_block`. 🔴 **This number cannot detect a dead chain**: both values freeze together when the sync stops, so a chain nine days dead publishes the same figure it had when it was healthy. Read `stale_hours` for that. Kept because it is the right measure of a scan that IS running.

last_sync_at.title: Last Sync At
last_sync_at.description: When the last successful sync of this chain finished. Null if it never synced.

stale_hours.title: Stale Hours
stale_hours.description: Hours since the last successful sync, **measured against the clock** — which is why it cannot lie in the direction `blocks_behind` lies in: a chain that stops syncing climbs on its own, tick after tick. Measured on two real cases: one chain nine days unindexed still published `blocks_behind: 647`, and another published a perfect **0** after five hours without syncing. **Null means it never synced** — unknown lag, not zero lag.

ChainStat.title: ChainStat
ChainStat.description:
El perfil de una cadena.

`avg_value` NUNCA viaja sola: `distinct_raters` y `top_rater_share` van al
lado en el mismo objeto, y esa es una decisión de producto, no de esquema.
Medido en este índice: avalanche promedia 76,95 y base 22,95, y el que lea
sólo esos dos números concluye que avalanche es mejor. La media de avalanche
sale de ONCE calificadores, con uno solo poniendo el 64 %; la de base, de
12.624. Publicar una media sin su N es el rumor que este sitio dice combatir.

El `example` del esquema es la fila REAL de solana leída del dominio el
2026-08-21 — no un payload inventado — y se eligió porque muestra el punto
de `stale_hours`: `blocks_behind` en 0 con casi ocho horas sin sincronizar.
La fila viva sale de `GET /chains`.

distinct_raters.title: Distinct Raters
distinct_raters.description: **How many wallets spoke.** Read it against `total_reviews`: this is the pair that separates consensus from repetition, and it is the one that catches what share alone misses.

top_client_share.title: Top Client Share
top_client_share.description: Fraction of the ratings written by the single loudest rater, 0-1. **Not the tell on its own** — the largest campaign in this index sits near 0.14, so any threshold on share alone waves it through. Null when there is no denominator.

top_client.title: Top Client
top_client.description: Address of that loudest rater, so the claim can be checked.

Concentration.title: Concentration
Concentration.description:
ADVISORY. Who the ratings came from. Never blocks, never moves a score.

Nullable ON PURPOSE, and consumers must handle the null: this is a
secondary aggregate, so when its query fails the endpoint drops the signal
rather than the answer. A reputation service that returns nothing because a
side-signal timed out has failed at its actual job.

`top_client_share` alone is not the tell. The campaign in this index — one
agent, 300.001 ratings, 57 raters, measured 2026-08-11 — sits near 0,14.
Read `distinct_raters` against `total_reviews`.

band.title: Band
band.description: How much evidence backs the score — **never the score itself**. `no_ratings` always travels beside a null score, never a zero. Branch on this value, which is a published enum; the wording of `advice` may change.

distinct_raters.title: Distinct Raters
distinct_raters.description: The N the band was computed from: distinct rating wallets, not ratings.

interval.description: Plausible range for the score. Null when the band is `no_ratings`: with no ratings the underlying function returns the whole 0-100 domain, and serialising a `lower: 0.0` next to a null score would publish a zero that is not a zero.

thresholds.title: Thresholds
thresholds.description: The cuts that produced the band, shipped with it so you can reproduce the banding without trusting a stale copy of the policy. Live values also at `GET /health.confidence_thresholds`.

advice.title: Advice
advice.description: One sentence on what to do with this much evidence. Prose, and it can change without notice — never branch on it, branch on `band`.

confidence_policy.title: Confidence Policy
confidence_policy.description: Version of the banding policy that produced this object, so a stored answer stays interpretable after the cuts move.

Confidence.title: Confidence
Confidence.description:
ADVISORY. How much evidence backs the number — never the number itself.

Nullable for exactly the same reason as `concentration`, and it goes null
with it: `distinct_raters` is read once, in SQL, and when that side query
degrades there is no N to band. A band invented over an N nobody could read
would be a label with no data under it.

`band == "no_ratings"` travels next to a **null** score, never a zero, and
`interval` is null there too: with no ratings the pure function returns the
whole domain (0-100) on purpose, but serialising a `lower: 0.0` beside a
null score would publish a 0 that is not a 0. Thresholds and policy version
ride along so the band can be reproduced without trusting a stale copy of
the cuts.

ConfidenceInterval.title: ConfidenceInterval
ConfidenceInterval.description: Wilson al 95 %, reescalado al dominio 0-100. NO es un score.

score.title: Score
score.description: Score for this area alone, 0-100, or **null** when there is nothing to average. Never coerce null to zero: a wallet nobody rated on `trust` is not a wallet rated badly on `trust`.

count.title: Count
count.description: Ratings in this area. Volume, not agreement.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: Rating direction as declared by the rater in `tag1` (`worker_rating`, `agent_rating`, `executor_rating`), or null when this facet declares none — which is the case for the vast majority of the index. Null means undeclared, not symmetric. Read `GET /stats/facets` free to measure the split yourself.

direction_category.title: Direction Category
direction_category.description: Task category the rater appended to the direction (`worker_rating:data_collection` -> `data_collection`), or null.

direction_meaning.title: Direction Meaning
direction_meaning.description: Plain-language translation of `direction`, declared by its emitter — Execution Market ratified it in writing on 2026-08-28 — never derived by this service: `publisher_rates_executor` (`worker_rating`) or `executor_rates_requester` (`agent_rating`, `executor_rating`). Null when `direction` is null or carries no ratified translation. Emitter's caveat: on the signed rail the buyer/seller labelling is best-effort and may degrade to requester/executor; the signer identity never does.

Facet.title: Facet
Facet.description:
One area of reputation, taken from the rater's `tag1`.

A wallet is not a number. `trust`, `liveness`, `contractRisk` and
`activity` are separate judgements that live side by side on chain, and a
caller picking a counterparty acts on the areas, not on their mean.

direction.title: Direction
direction.description: Rating direction declared by the rater in `tag1`, or null when this facet declares none. Null means undeclared, not symmetric.

direction_category.title: Direction Category
direction_category.description: Task category appended to the direction, or null.

direction_meaning.title: Direction Meaning
direction_meaning.description: Plain-language translation of `direction`, declared by its emitter (Execution Market, ratified in writing 2026-08-28), never derived here: `publisher_rates_executor` or `executor_rates_requester`. Null when `direction` is null or carries no ratified translation.

FacetStat.title: FacetStat
FacetStat.description:
A facet across the whole index.

`distinct_agents` is what separates a facet from a campaign: volume alone
ranks a single-target vouching run above every honest signal there is.

network.title: Network
network.description: Chain the rating was written on.

agent_id.title: Agent Id
agent_id.description: ERC-8004 identity that was rated, within its chain. The pair (network, agent_id) is what identifies a subject.

rater.title: Rater
rater.description: Wallet that wrote the rating. A public address already on chain — what never travels here is free text one party wrote about another.

subject_wallet.title: Subject Wallet
subject_wallet.description: Owner of the rated identity, or **null** when we do not know who owns it today. Null is not «has no owner»: the Reputation scan can run ahead of the Identity one.

value.title: Value
value.description: The rating as written on chain, unmodified. This is evidence, not a score: no weighting, no shrinkage, no policy.

facet.title: Facet
facet.description: Area of reputation the rater declared (`tag1`), or null when they declared none.

block_time.title: Block Time
block_time.description: **On-chain** time of the rating, never when we indexed it. Dating a historical rating with our own ingestion timestamp would make every backfilled rating look like it happened today.

tx_hash.title: Tx Hash
tx_hash.description: Transaction that carries this rating, so you can verify it against the chain instead of trusting us. Null only where the backfill has not reached yet.

FeedEvent.title: FeedEvent
FeedEvent.description:
Una calificación que ya ocurrió en un bloque finalizado.

El `example` del esquema es un evento REAL del feed, leído del dominio el
2026-08-21: su `tx_hash` se puede abrir en un explorador, que es todo el
punto de este producto. `block_time` lo fecha solo.

status.title: Status
status.description: `ok` when the service answered. Liveness, not a claim about coverage.

policy_version.title: Policy Version
policy_version.description: Version of the SCORE policy: equal weight per chain, value domain, revoked out, join by the identity's current owner. It is the one that travels in every scored response.

ordering_policy.title: Ordering Policy
ordering_policy.description: Version of how the leaderboard is ORDERED (Bayesian shrinkage). It never changes a published score — only the sort.

rater_weight_policy.title: Rater Weight Policy
rater_weight_policy.description: Version of the second weighting published beside every score as `weighted_score`. Advisory: it is not the served number.

confidence_policy.title: Confidence Policy
confidence_policy.description: Version of the evidence bands. Names how much evidence backs a number without touching the number. **The four versions are separate because they change separately**: fusing them would mark every rating as recomputed each time a list is edited, and then the score's own version would stop meaning anything.

confidence_thresholds.title: Confidence Thresholds
confidence_thresholds.description: The distinct-rater cuts of each confidence band, here and free. This is what lets a consumer of the FREE `/leaderboard` — which already receives `distinct_raters` — derive the exact band without paying, and it is why the band is not repeated on every row: repeating a derivable string a hundred times adds bytes to a cached response, not a fact.

reading_policy.title: Reading Policy
reading_policy.description: The **effective** cuts that fire a `caveats[]` entry, so a surface can READ them instead of typing them. This is the mechanism that keeps an environment override from being an invisible drift: the value actually in force is always legible here, free and without an account. Not a fifth policy and deliberately unversioned — it moves no score and no price. Left as a free-form object because its owner is the caveats module: a new cut has to reach whoever reads it without waiting for this file to catch up. A null inside IS data — `self_gap` is null because there is no self-rating threshold, the gap is always published.

build_sha.title: Build Sha
build_sha.description: Git commit the running code was built from (stamped into the artifact at build time), or null when the build was not stamped.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: Agent identities indexed right now, across every chain. **Live and uncached** — this is the authoritative total, and the reason no page in this product types one.

feedback_entries.title: Feedback Entries
feedback_entries.description: Individual ratings indexed right now — the grain everything else aggregates over. Live and uncached, same rule as `agents`.

indexer_period_seconds.title: Indexer Period Seconds
indexer_period_seconds.description: How often the indexer runs, in seconds, as the running service has it configured — or null when the environment does not declare it. Null means unknown, never a guessed cadence.

chains.title: Chains
chains.description: One row per indexed chain, straight from the indexer's own sync state. Stable fields: `network` (the vocabulary for every `{network}` path parameter), `last_scanned_block`, `head_at_last_sync`, `started_at`, `updated_at` (when the last successful sync finished — the field that ages when a chain dies), and `last_error`. Chains scanned by signature instead of block number (solana) also carry `newest_signature`, `oldest_signature` and `backfill_complete`. Plus `next_sync_at`, computed here and not stored: `updated_at` plus `indexer_period_seconds`, or null when either is missing. A `next_sync_at` already in the past is not a bug — it means the tick that was due has not landed, which is exactly what you want it to say. For staleness measured against the clock, read `stale_hours` in `GET /chains`.

Health.title: Health
Health.description:
Liveness, index size and every policy in force — live, free and uncached.

🔴 **This route is the authority on every figure about this index.** No
total is typed by hand anywhere else in this API, on the site or in the
docs: indexing runs continuously, and a number written into a document goes
stale while still sounding exact. Ask here instead.

It is also where the effective value of every tunable parameter is
published, which is what keeps an environment override auditable rather
than an invisible drift.

HistoryCoverage.title: HistoryCoverage
HistoryCoverage.description:
How much of the wallet's reputation the series could actually plot.

Ratings without `block_time` are excluded from every point — the log scan
has not dated them yet. Reported instead of hidden: while
`undated_reviews > 0` the last point of the series is legitimately below
`final_score`, and without this field that gap reads as a bug.

HistoryPoint.title: HistoryPoint
HistoryPoint.description:
One bucket of the time series.

`score` is what that period's ratings said; `cumulative_score` is the score
computed over everything up to and including it — the number the API would
have served on that date. They answer different questions and the graph
needs both: the first is spiky by nature, the second is the trend line.

IssuerNoHost.title: IssuerNoHost
IssuerNoHost.description: The coverage bucket: ratings whose URI names no http(s) host.

issuer_host.title: Issuer Host
issuer_host.description: Host of `feedbackURI`, lowercased and without `www.` — the service this rating was published from. A fact of the URI, never a judgement.

issuer.title: Issuer
issuer.description: Canonical name when the host is a known Ultravioleta DAO product (allowlist, never inferred), else null. Null does NOT mean unknown issuer — `issuer_host` is the issuer.

issuer_org.title: Issuer Org
issuer_org.description: `uvd` when this issuer is a product of the house, else null. This route is how you audit how much of the index its own operators wrote.

IssuerStat.title: IssuerStat
IssuerStat.description:
One issuing service, with the reach that says what its volume is made of.

`distinct_agents`/`distinct_raters` beside `count` are what separate a
public from a campaign, and the cut by WHO WRITES is where they bite
hardest: measured 2026-08-29, the loudest issuer here is 301,180 ratings
on 16 agents, and the second is 48,852 ratings over 7,436 agents signed by
exactly 3 raters.

no_host.description: Ratings with no http(s) host in `feedbackURI` (`data:`, `ipfs:`, empty). Absent provenance is data, not a hole: this bucket is how much of the index declares no issuing service at all.

IssuerStats.title: IssuerStats
IssuerStats.description:
Who wrote the index: the hosts that emitted the ratings we read.

Advisory and descriptive — an issuer's volume moves no score. It is
published so a reader can see how concentrated the evidence is.

rank.title: Rank
rank.description: Position in this ordering, 1-based. It comes from `shrunk_score`, not from `final_score`.

final_score.title: Final Score
final_score.description: The observed mean, untouched — the same number the paid wallet route serves. **It is not what decides the position.** Null, never 0, with no eligible ratings.

shrunk_score.title: Shrunk Score
shrunk_score.description: **What decides the position**: the Bayesian mean — the observed score pulled toward the index prior by how many distinct raters back it, so four glowing ratings cannot outrank four hundred. Null when the index cannot form a prior.

distinct_raters.title: Distinct Raters
distinct_raters.description: The N of that formula: **distinct raters, not ratings**. Without it `shrunk_score` cannot be recomputed by hand and the order is not auditable. It is also what lets a free caller derive the confidence band without paying — the cuts are in `GET /health`, which is why the band is not repeated on every row.

chain_count.title: Chain Count
chain_count.description: How many chains contributed a score to this wallet.

networks.title: Networks
networks.description: **Which** chains the wallet has a score on, not just how many. Without it a UI can say '3 chains' and not which — and one icon per network is the fastest way to read a profile that spans them.

declared_types.title: Declared Types
declared_types.description: The types declared by this wallet's identities. `null` is a legitimate member of the list: it means an identity that declares no type, which is common.

LeaderboardRow.title: LeaderboardRow
LeaderboardRow.description:
One row of the ranking, carrying the numbers that produced its position.

The row publishes BOTH scores and the N between them on purpose: a list
ordered by a number it does not show is a list you have to believe. With
these three fields the order can be recomputed by hand.

Manifesto.title: Manifesto
Manifesto.description:
The principles this service is built on, machine-readable.

Static: it never touches the index, so it costs nothing to serve and
cannot go stale against a number.

ManifestoPrinciple.title: ManifestoPrinciple
ManifestoPrinciple.description: One principle, with what enforces it in the code.

ManifestoVerification.title: ManifestoVerification
ManifestoVerification.description: One claim and the exact command that checks it from outside.

owner_updated_block.title: Owner Updated Block
owner_updated_block.description: The block the handover happened at — the line that splits the two eras. Every rating below it was earned by somebody else.

identity_transferred.title: Identity Transferred
identity_transferred.description: Whether the identity actually changed hands. **Not derivable from the counts**, which is why it travels: `inherited_review_count == 0` means two different things — the identity never moved, or it moved and nobody had rated it yet — and telling them apart is what this field is for. Null when no `Registered` row is indexed for it.

inherited_review_count.title: Inherited Review Count
inherited_review_count.description: Eligible ratings that landed BEFORE the handover.

inherited_score.title: Inherited Score
inherited_score.description: Mean over those. Null when there are none.

current_era_review_count.title: Current Era Review Count
current_era_review_count.description: Eligible ratings SINCE the handover. 'Current era' means since the last transfer, not since the mint: no Transfer history is kept, so an identity that changed hands three times publishes one era.

current_era_score.title: Current Era Score
current_era_score.description: Mean over those. Null when there are none.

undetermined_review_count.title: Undetermined Review Count
undetermined_review_count.description: Eligible ratings the log scan has not dated yet, so neither era can claim them. **They are not distributed to either side** — guessing would be the cheap lie. This is why the three counts sum to `review_count` exactly.

inherited_share.title: Inherited Share
inherited_share.description: Inherited fraction of the dated ratings, 0-1. Null with a zero denominator: a `0.0` would read as 'inherited nothing', which is a claim with no data behind it.

Ownership.title: Ownership
Ownership.description:
ADVISORY. What today's owner earned of this score, and what it inherited.

The split is the rating's `block_number` against the identity's
`owner_updated_block`: whatever landed before the handover was earned by
somebody else. It exists because without it a bought reputation — mint, get
rated, transfer — is indistinguishable from an earned one, and that is the
cheapest attack there is on an index like this one.

**It never moves `score`.** Both averages break down exactly the population
that produced `review_count`, which is why `inherited_review_count +
current_era_review_count + undetermined_review_count == review_count` adds
up by hand.

NULL MEANS "THE ERA CANNOT BE ESTABLISHED", NEVER "NOTHING WAS INHERITED".
It is null when there is no identity row, when `owner_updated_block` is
NULL, and **always on `solana`**: there that column is not the position of a
Transfer but the SLOT AT WHICH THE INDEXER READ the asset (ownership in
Metaplex Core is present state, not an event), so the predicate would flag
100,00 % of that chain's ratings as inherited — every single one. Publishing
that would accuse a whole network over a column-semantics bug.

AND IT IS NOT A VERDICT: a business sale, a custody migration or a wallet
rotation produce exactly the same figure as a bought reputation. The field
publishes counts and averages; the judgement is the reader's.

pricing_version.title: Pricing Version
pricing_version.description: Version of this whole table. It bumps on any price change **and on any move of the free/paid line**, and it rides in every 402 and in the `X-Pricing-Version` header — read it from there rather than pinning a copy.

networks.title: Networks
networks.description: Chains accepted for payment, **in the order challenges offer them**: the first entry of `accepts[]` in every 402 is the first network of this list.

free_tier.title: Free Tier
free_tier.description: What the free tier is, in one line, so the free/paid boundary is legible without diffing the table.

tiers.title: Tiers
tiers.description: Every priced route. This is the same table the paywall charges from — published, not a copy of it.

PricingCatalog.title: PricingCatalog
PricingCatalog.description:
La forma de `paywall.catalog()` — lo que se publica ES lo que se cobra.

El handler no arma este objeto: lo entrega el paywall montado, y este
modelo solo lo declara para el esquema. Un campo nuevo en `catalog()` tiene
que agregarse acá o no sale publicado — que es la dirección correcta del
error: mejor un campo que falta que un catálogo que diverge del cobro.

id.title: Id
id.description: Stable identifier of the tier. It also travels in every 402 as `pricing.tier`, so a client can match the challenge it got against this table.

path.title: Path
path.description: The route as a regex over the request path — the very pattern the middleware matches, published unaltered so you can replay the match instead of guessing which tier a URL falls into.

price_usd.title: Price Usd
price_usd.description: Price in USD **as a string, never a float**: a price that JSON rounds on its own cannot be reconciled against what was settled on-chain. Parse it as a decimal.

free.title: Free
free.description: Whether this route answers with no payment. The line is a cost rule, not a mood: free is what a cache serves to everybody, paid is what only you asked for.

conditional.title: Conditional
conditional.description: True when the price depends on the query string (`?snapshot=true` is the one left after the leaderboard split by path). When true, the authoritative price for one concrete call is that call's own 402 — not this row.

why.title: Why
why.description: The cost reason behind the price, in one sentence. It also travels inside every 402: a charge that cannot explain its own number is indistinguishable from an invented one.

PricingTier.title: PricingTier
PricingTier.description: One row of the table the paywall actually charges from.

RaterChain.title: RaterChain
RaterChain.description: One chain where this wallet acted as a RATER, not as a subject.

wallet.title: Wallet
wallet.description: The wallet, read as the author of ratings rather than their subject.

ratings_emitted.title: Ratings Emitted
ratings_emitted.description: Every rating this wallet wrote, revoked and out-of-domain included.

revoked_count.title: Revoked Count
revoked_count.description: How many of them it later took back.

eligible_count.title: Eligible Count
eligible_count.description: The ones that survive the same eligibility rules the scores use. The denominator of `value_avg` and `value_stddev`.

self_ratings.title: Self Ratings
self_ratings.description: Ratings this wallet wrote over agents it OWNS. **Not excluded** from the aggregates here — surfaced so you can subtract them yourself, which is the opposite of the rated side, where they are excluded from every score.

distinct_subjects.title: Distinct Subjects
distinct_subjects.description: How many different agents it rated. Read against `ratings_emitted`: a big ratio is a rater talking about the whole index, a small one is a rater talking about one thing.

value_avg.title: Value Avg
value_avg.description: Mean value this rater hands out. **Null, never 0**, with no eligible ratings: 'emitted nothing' and 'emitted all zeros' are different facts.

value_stddev.title: Value Stddev
value_stddev.description: Dispersion of those values. **A rater stamping the same number on everything has stddev 0** — we surface it, we do not verdict it. Null when there is nothing to disperse.

first_rating_at.title: First Rating At
first_rating_at.description: First rating written, by on-chain time. Null until the log scan dates it.

last_rating_at.title: Last Rating At
last_rating_at.description: Last rating written, by on-chain time. Null until the log scan dates it.

top_subject_share.title: Top Subject Share
top_subject_share.description: Fraction of this rater's ACTIVE ratings landing on its favourite subject — the mirror of `top_client_share` on the rated side. `1.0` means everything went to one agent. Null with nothing eligible.

per_chain.title: Per Chain
per_chain.description: The same activity split by chain, never collapsed into a total.

roles.title: Roles
roles.description: How many ratings it wrote under each declared role, read from `tag1` through the SAME allowlist the facet `direction` uses — one policy, one owner. Never by splitting the tag on `:`: this index carries hundreds of distinct tags and a split would invent roles that outweigh the real ones.

unknown_tag_count.title: Unknown Tag Count
unknown_tag_count.description: Ratings whose `tag1` matches no declared role. **Data, not errors** — most of the index declares no role at all.

policy_version.title: Policy Version
policy_version.description: The aggregation policy behind these figures. Also in `GET /health`.

RaterProfile.title: RaterProfile
RaterProfile.description:
The wallet as RATER: its emitted ratings, decomposed. No score.

Deliberately: ranking raters would be a NEW verdict ("this publisher is
trustworthy"), and this index returns evidence, not verdicts. You get the
activity decomposed -- volume, distinct subjects, dispersion,
concentration, roles -- and YOU decide what it means.

client.title: Client
client.description: Who wrote this rating: the rater's address. This is the field the whole product is about — a score without its raters is a rumor.

feedback_index.title: Feedback Index
feedback_index.description: The rater's own counter for this subject, part of the natural key `(network, agent_id, client, feedback_index)`. It is what makes re-indexing idempotent.

value.title: Value
value.description: The raw on-chain integer, untouched. Read it together with `value_decimals`; use `normalized_value` for anything comparable.

value_decimals.title: Value Decimals
value_decimals.description: Decimal places the emitter declared for `value`.

normalized_value.title: Normalized Value
normalized_value.description: `value` brought to the 0-100 domain — the only figure comparable across emitters. Null when the row is out of domain, which is also why it was excluded from the score.

tag1.title: Tag1
tag1.description: The rater's first tag: the AREA being judged (`trust`, `liveness`, `contractRisk`, `activity`, …) and, when the emitter declares it, the direction prefix. This is what `facets` are keyed by. Free vocabulary — the index carries hundreds of distinct values, so read it, never split it on `:` and hope.

tag2.title: Tag2
tag2.description: The rater's second tag, if any.

is_revoked.title: Is Revoked
is_revoked.description: The rater took this rating back. Excluded from every score, returned anyway — with `revoked_tx` — because a revocation nobody can audit is not a revocation.

is_self.title: Is Self
is_self.description: The rater IS the rated agent's current owner. Attribution, not eligibility: it travels on every row — revoked and out-of-domain included — so the breakdown says where each point came from without the caller recomputing the comparison. Self-ratings are out of every score and summarised in `self_rated`.

tx_hash.title: Tx Hash
tx_hash.description: The transaction that wrote this rating — go verify it in an explorer, which is the point. **Null until the log scan reaches this entry**, not null forever.

block_number.title: Block Number
block_number.description: Block the rating landed in. Null until the log scan dates it.

log_index.title: Log Index
log_index.description: Position within the block. Null until the log scan dates it.

feedback_uri.title: Feedback Uri
feedback_uri.description: The `feedbackURI` the standard carries — where the rater published the rating. The three `issuer*` fields below are read from it.

issuer_host.title: Issuer Host
issuer_host.description: Host of `feedback_uri`, lowercased and without `www.` — where this rating was published. Null when the rating carries no http(s) URI. Present for ~82% of the index.

issuer.title: Issuer
issuer.description: Canonical name of the issuing product when the host is a known Ultravioleta DAO service (e.g. `execution-market`), else null. Null does NOT mean unknown issuer — read `issuer_host` for that.

issuer_org.title: Issuer Org
issuer_org.description: `uvd` when this rating was written by an Ultravioleta DAO product, else null. One stable label, independent of how many products there are or what each is called.

feedback_hash.title: Feedback Hash
feedback_hash.description: Content hash the rater committed to, when it declared one.

revoked_tx.title: Revoked Tx
revoked_tx.description: The transaction that killed this rating. Without it a revocation is unauditable — which is why it travels instead of the row simply disappearing.

Rating.title: Rating
Rating.description:
One individual rating, exactly as it was written on chain.

This is the grain of the whole index — every score in this API is an
aggregate over rows of this shape, and the paid agent route returns them
one by one, revoked ones included, each with the transaction that proves
it. A revocation nobody can audit is not a revocation.

SearchMatch.title: SearchMatch
SearchMatch.description:
Una fila que el índice reconoció, con la LECTURA bajo la cual la encontró.

`interpreted_as` viaja por fila y no en la raíz porque un mismo string
base58 puede ser wallet Y asset a la vez: `wallet_chains` lo toma como
wallet de Solana y `agent_reputation` lo toma como asset de Metaplex Core —
dos sujetos distintos, con dueños distintos, escritos igual. Fundir las dos
lecturas en una etiqueta de raíz borraría cuál produjo cuál.

query.title: Query
query.description: Exactly what you sent, untouched. It is the only thing that lets you see you pasted a trailing space or an invisible character.

normalized_query.title: Normalized Query
normalized_query.description: What we actually looked up. It differs from `query` only for EVM input, which is lowercased; a base58 travels byte for byte, because lowercasing it would silently invent a different key.

matches.title: Matches
matches.description: What the index knows under that string. An empty list with a non-empty `interpretations` means the shape was valid and nothing matched — not that the query was wrong.

SearchResult.title: SearchResult
SearchResult.description:
Lo que la caja entendió y dónde lo encontró, en dos capas separadas.

La separación ES el diseño: `interpretations` (raíz) es lo que la **forma**
permite —léxico, barato, no toca la base—, y `matches[].interpreted_as` es
bajo qué lectura el **índice** encontró esa fila. Una entrada puede tener dos
interpretaciones y cero matches, o una interpretación y once matches.

**No existe el valor `"ambiguous"` y no hay un `ambiguous: bool`.** La señal
de ambigüedad es `len(interpretations) > 1`, que además dice CUÁLES son;
colapsarlas en una etiqueta borra esa información, que es el modo de falla
que este repo persigue.

El `example` del esquema es una respuesta REAL, leída del índice el
2026-08-23 — no una maqueta. Es un base58 de Solana a propósito: la forma
admite dos lecturas (`interpretations` trae dos) y el índice sólo encontró
filas bajo una (`matches` trae una, `interpreted_as: solana_asset`), y ese
desfase entre las dos capas es justamente lo que un ejemplo con una sola
interpretación no muestra. Su `refreshed_at` en `null` también es real: esta
fila salió del grano vivo, no de una vista materializada.

SelfRated.title: SelfRated
SelfRated.description:
Lo que el sujeto dice de si mismo — excluido del score, no del perfil.

`gap` = self - others. Positivo significa que se sobrevalora. Es la lectura
mas informativa del perfil y sale gratis del predicado que ya excluye la
autocalificacion del promedio.

inputs_digest.title: Inputs Digest
inputs_digest.description: Digest of the inputs the answer was computed from. Two snapshots with the same digest and the same `policy_version` say the same thing — this is what makes an answer citable.

policy_version.title: Policy Version
policy_version.description: Aggregation policy in force when this was computed. Without it a stored score cannot be interpreted after the rules move.

Snapshot.title: Snapshot
Snapshot.description:
A stored answer with the digest and policy version it was computed under.

It exists so a decision made on this data can be re-read later and
still mean the same thing.

classification_source.title: Classification Source
classification_source.description: Where the types came from. They are **declared** by each identity and never verified by us: a declaration is not a fact, and most identities declare nothing.

types.title: Types
types.description: One entry per declared type. The `unknown` bucket is the largest by a wide margin and means «did not say», never «we could not classify it».

TypeBreakdown.title: TypeBreakdown
TypeBreakdown.description:
The index split by declared agent type.

Most identities declare nothing, so the unknown bucket is the largest
by a wide margin — read it as «did not say», never as
«unclassified by us».

rated_agent_count.title: Rated Agent Count
rated_agent_count.description: How many of them have any rating at all. The rest have no score — not a score of zero.

avg_score.title: Avg Score
avg_score.description: Mean across the rated ones, or null when none are rated.

TypeStats.title: TypeStats
TypeStats.description:
Aggregate for one declared agent type.

The type is what the identity SAYS it is, taken verbatim from its own
card. We never verify it.

network.title: Network
network.description: Chain this row is about, by our own name for it. The full list is in `GET /health.chains` — that is the authority.

agent_count.title: Agent Count
agent_count.description: How many ERC-8004 identities this wallet owns on this chain. **Zero means something different from absent**: there are ratings here but we have not indexed the registry that issued them.

agent_ids.title: Agent Ids
agent_ids.description: The identity ids themselves, to feed `GET /reputation/agent/{network}/{id}`. Null when the row came from a materialised view that does not carry them.

final_score.title: Final Score
final_score.description: Score on this chain, 0-100, or **null**. Null is not zero: an identity with no ratings has no score, and a zero would be asserting somebody rated it badly. Branch on null, never coerce it.

total_reviews.title: Total Reviews
total_reviews.description: Ratings counted on this chain. Volume, not agreement — read it next to `distinct_raters`.

distinct_raters.title: Distinct Raters
distinct_raters.description: How many distinct wallets did the rating, which is the number that separates evidence from a campaign. 642 ratings from 467 raters and 642 from one rater are the same `total_reviews` and not remotely the same fact.

WalletChain.title: WalletChain
WalletChain.description: Una cadena en la que esta wallet existe, tenga o no reputación ahí.

wallet.title: Wallet
wallet.description: The wallet asked about, normalised. EVM addresses come back lowercased; Solana keeps its base58 case.

chains.title: Chains
chains.description: One row per chain where this wallet exists, whether or not it has reputation there. An empty list means «not registered anywhere we index» — which is an answer, not an error.

caveats.title: Caveats
caveats.description: SUBSET of the caveats: only those computable from public data without touching the grain (today: `burn-address`, for well-known burn addresses -- nobody controls them, nobody can answer for their reputation). The full evidence-quality set (concentration, single rater, campaign...) travels ONLY in the paid decomposition `GET /reputation/wallet/{wallet}`. An empty list here means 'no public-data caveat', NOT 'no caveats at all'.

identity_count.title: Identity Count
identity_count.description: Total ERC-8004 identities this wallet owns across every chain we read.

chains_with_identity.title: Chains With Identity
chains_with_identity.description: On how many chains it holds at least one identity.

chains_with_reputation.title: Chains With Reputation
chains_with_reputation.description: On how many of those it actually has ratings. The gap against `chains_with_identity` is registered-but-unrated, which is a different fact from unregistered.

total_reviews.title: Total Reviews
total_reviews.description: Ratings across every chain. Volume, not agreement.

distinct_raters.title: Distinct Raters
distinct_raters.description: Distinct raters across the WHOLE wallet, deduplicated between chains. **Do not sum `chains[].distinct_raters`** — the same rater can rate on several chains and the sum double-counts them (measured: a wallet whose per-chain counts add to 10 has 9 real raters). `null` means the wallet is not in the ranking, which is not the same as zero raters.

WalletChains.title: WalletChains
WalletChains.description:
El mapa gratis de una wallet: identidades y reputación por cadena.

El `example` del esquema es la respuesta REAL del dominio para la wallet
del ejemplo de la ruta, leída el 2026-08-21 — su `refreshed_at` la fecha
solo. La respuesta viva es la de la propia ruta, que es gratis.

wallet.title: Wallet
wallet.description: The wallet this history is about.

bucket.title: Bucket
bucket.description: Size of each time bucket the points are grouped into.

points.title: Points
points.description: One point per bucket, by **on-chain** time — never by when we indexed it.

coverage.description: How much of the range we can actually speak for. Read it before reading the curve: a gap here is missing evidence, not a drop in reputation.

WalletHistory.title: WalletHistory
WalletHistory.description:
How a wallet's reputation moved over time, bucketed by on-chain time.

Read `coverage` before the curve: a flat stretch can be a quiet
period or a range we cannot speak for, and those are different facts.

wallet.title: Wallet
wallet.description: The subject, echoed back as it was resolved. EVM addresses come back lowercased (the grain guarantees it); Solana base58 ids keep their case, because there case IS identity.

final_score.title: Final Score
final_score.description: The published score, 0-100: the **mean of the per-chain scores**, one vote per chain, so a chain carrying hundreds of thousands of ratings cannot drown one carrying four. Revoked, out-of-domain and self-ratings are out of it. **Null, never 0**, when there is no eligible rating: no data is not bad data.

weighted_score.title: Weighted Score
weighted_score.description: The SAME grain under a second weighting (`rater_weight_policy`), published beside the served number rather than replacing it. **It is not the policy**: `final_score` is what this API serves and what a snapshot records. It travels because changing how hundreds of thousands of ratings are weighted is not something a reputation index gets to do silently. Null means two different things and `final_score` tells them apart: if that one has a number and this one does not, the side signal degraded; if both are null, the wallet has no evidence.

rater_weight_policy.title: Rater Weight Policy
rater_weight_policy.description: Version string of the weighting that produced `weighted_score`. Also published free in `GET /health`.

chain_count.title: Chain Count
chain_count.description: How many chains contributed a score — the size of the vote in the mean above, not how many chains the wallet merely appears on.

total_reviews.title: Total Reviews
total_reviews.description: Eligible ratings behind the score, summed across chains. Read it against `concentration.distinct_raters`: the two together are what separates consensus from repetition.

per_chain.title: Per Chain
per_chain.description: The score per chain, never collapsed — keyed by network. This is the breakdown the mean above is made of, so the mean can be recomputed by hand.

facets.title: Facets
facets.description: Reputation by area, keyed by the rater's `tag1` — `trust`, `liveness`, `contractRisk` and `activity` are separate judgements, not a mean. **Ordered by volume desc**: dict order is the ranking, so a client can take the first N without re-sorting. The overall score and one facet can disagree by more than 30 points on the same wallet, and that gap is the product.

self_rated.description: What the subject said about itself — excluded from every score above, published here instead of hidden. `gap = self - others`: positive means it overrates itself.

concentration.description: ADVISORY, and **nullable on purpose**: this is a secondary aggregate, so when its query degrades the endpoint drops the signal rather than the answer. Never moves a score.

confidence.description: ADVISORY band over how much evidence backs the number — never the number itself. Goes null together with `concentration`, and for the same reason: the band is computed over `distinct_raters`, and a band invented over an N nobody could read would be a label with no data under it.

activity.description: First and last rating **by on-chain time**, never by when we indexed the row.

caveats.title: Caveats
caveats.description: The traps THESE numbers trigger, already written out. Derived from the fields of this same response — `final_score`, `total_reviews`, `concentration`, `self_rated` — never from a second query, which is why it costs nothing extra. **Advisory: it never moves the score and never fills a null one.** An empty list means no trap fired, NOT 'verified clean'. Each entry is `{code, text}`: branch on `code`, which is permanent; `text` is Spanish prose meant to be shown to whoever is deciding and may be rewritten or re-measured without notice. Same objects the MCP tool `describe_lookup_wallet` returns: one policy, two doors.

policy_version.title: Policy Version
policy_version.description: The aggregation policy that produced these numbers. It travels in every scored response so two callers can never be served different numbers without the difference being visible, and so a stored number can be traced back to the rules that made it.

snapshot.description: Only on `?snapshot=true`: the durable receipt row that was written, with its `inputs_digest` and `policy_version` — something you can hand a counterparty and we can recompute identically. Null on a plain read, which writes nothing.

WalletScore.title: WalletScore
WalletScore.description:
One wallet's reputation, decomposed into what produced it.

The headline number is `final_score`, but it is the least interesting field
here: everything beside it exists so the number can be checked instead of
believed — which chains it came from, which areas disagree, how many
distinct counterparties are behind it, and what the subject says about
itself.

x402.name: X-PAYMENT
x402.description:
**Payment is the authentication.** There is no account, no API key and nothing to register: the credential for a metered call is a base64 x402 payload carrying an EIP-3009 USDC authorization that YOU sign locally — no private key ever leaves your side.

How to get one: call the operation with no header at all. It answers **402** with the challenge (asking is free and is the intended first move), you sign `accepts[]` — the only thing you sign against — and you replay the identical request with this header. The 200 comes back with `X-Payment-Receipt`.

Two properties no `apiKey` scheme can express, so read them here: the credential is **per call** (the nonce is consumed at settlement, so it will not pay twice) and a receipt is reusable only for the byte-identical resource — wallet A's receipt cannot unlock wallet B. Full contract: https://describe.net/auth.md

tags.name: Free
tags.description: No payment, no headers, no account. Two kinds, one cost rule: the aggregate view of the index (one query that serves everybody) and the per-subject previews a cache serves to everyone asking the same thing (`/wallets/{wallet}/chains`, `/search/{query}`, `/badge/{wallet}.svg`) — either way the marginal caller costs nothing. Start here: reading these tells you whether the metered tier is worth it.

externalDocs.description: The API guide, with worked calls

tags.name: Metered (x402)
tags.description: Answers a question about one named subject. Returns **HTTP 402 with a signable challenge** until paid; calling it unpaid is free and is the intended first move. See **How to pay** at the top of this page — and pay only the address published there.

externalDocs.description: How to authenticate — i.e. how to pay

tags.name: Agent protocols
tags.description: The same index behind a protocol instead of behind a route: **MCP** (Streamable HTTP) and **A2A** (JSON-RPC 2.0), each on a single POST path. Free at the door and priced underneath — the MCP server neither charges nor signs nor holds a key: it relays the 402 of the route behind the tool and forwards the credential **you** signed. Listed here because an agent that only reads this schema had no way to discover either one.
